system.description:
Prerequisites: Advanced Animalism, Advanced Vicissitude. While the creation of vozhd was once the sole province of koldunic ritual, Tzimisce who have mastered both fleshcrafting and control of the Beast Within can build vozhd unaided. The ingredients: at least 15 ghouls (20 or more is preferable). The Tzimisce first fleshcrafts the ghouls together, forging the bodies into a single entity, then feeds the corporate mess a concoction of the blood of all the ghouls, creating something like a Vinculum among them. With this bond in place, the Fiend uses Animalism to coalesce the Beasts of the ghouls into one insane, imperfect Beast that drives the vozhd to crush or devour everything in sight.

System: After the Tzimisce collects enough ghouls, roll Intelligence + Body Craft (difficulty 10) to determine how quickly she constructs and "masters" the vozhd; with one success the process takes as long as a year, with five it might take only a month. The Fiend can make further Vicissitude modifications to her creation (raise the difficulty of such rolls by two to reflect the size and complexity of the creature). Botches result in a nonviable biohazard or a frenzied, uncontrollable vozhd; vozhd are notoriously difficult to control, raising the difficulty of all Animalism rolls involving one by three. Costs 36 experience points to learn.

MET System: First enter a Hard Test against the Storyteller. Should you lose, you must wait a year before attempting Birth the Vozhd again, representing the physical and spiritual strength this power requires. You may reduce the waiting period by spending a Willpower Trait for each month by which you wish to decrease it; once spent, these Traits cannot be used again until the waiting period concludes. Live-action Storytellers are encouraged to disallow this power for player characters and reserve vozhd for when the story requires one, given how difficult the process is to simulate in that medium.
system.source: Clanbook: Tzimisce, Chapter Two: Ego and Evolution
